_comment: UHS overrides to HPG's region/period table, applied after it by scripts/port-name-kits.ts. `replace` drops every HPG window for that region and uses these instead; `add` keeps HPG's and merges these in, clipping any HPG window that overlaps. Keys are UHS region ids as they appear in name-regions.generated.ts. Windows are [from, to), astronomical years, half-open.

european-ural-mountains.why: HPG gave the whole Urals Scandinavian names for 200-1200 and proto-Germanic before that, which is 2000 km and a language family out. The middle and northern Urals are Permic and Ob-Ugric country, with Turkic pressure from the south after the Bulgar and Horde periods.

european-ural-and-arctic-europe.why: Same fault further north. This is Nenets, Komi and Sami country; Russian settlement follows the sixteenth century.

european-lapland.why: HPG gave Lapland proto-Germanic and then Scandinavian. Sapmi is Sami; Nordic names arrive with church and state registration.

european-scandinavia.why: The Viking age and the high Middle Ages were running on a modern Swedish pool. Old Norse covers the migration period to 1700; the modern pool is now clamped to 1700.

european-atlantic-islands.why: Iceland and the Faroes were uninhabited before the ninth century, so the window should start at settlement rather than at the beginning of time.

european-british-isles.why: Scandinavian settlement in the Danelaw and the Isles was Old Norse-speaking, not modern Swedish.

east-asian-japan.why: One window from the beginning of time to the present, on a pool of Meiji-era surnames. Japan was settled deep in the Palaeolithic but its onomastics are not recoverable before the written record.

southeast-asian-indochina-interior.why: Angkor was running on modern Cambodian names with Sino-Cambodian surnames.

east-asian-kazakh-steppes.why: Ottoman names were standing in for the Turk and Uyghur khaganates and the whole pre-Mongol steppe.

east-asian-xinjiang.why: As the Kazakh steppes; the Uyghur khaganate and its successors are the Old Turkic case proper.

east-asian-siberia.why: Siberia had no coverage at all between the deep-time pool and the Russian conquest, which is four thousand years of the largest region in the atlas.

sub-saharan-african-southern-africa.why: Great Zimbabwe and Mutapa fell in the hole left by clamping the modern Zulu, Xhosa and Shona pools to 1900.

sub-saharan-african-sahel.why: Wagadu and the pre-Mali Sahel fell in the hole left by clamping west-african-sahel to 1200.

southeast-asian-philippines.why: The Philippines had no window at all before Spanish arrival in 1565, so forty thousand years and the Manila and Butuan polities produced invented syllables.

european-italy.why: Ostrogothic and Lombard Italy was running on modern German names with modern German surnames.

european-germanic-lands.why: The Rhine and the Elbe between Rome and the Carolingians, and the medieval German lands after them.

european-transylvania.why: Gothic and Gepid Transylvania, then the medieval kingdom.

mena-nile-valley.why: HPG ran one prehistoric window from 3100 BCE to Alexander, so three thousand years of dynastic Egypt — the best-attested name corpus in the ancient world — produced invented prehistoric names. Split by the conventional dynastic periods, with Greek and then Roman names added where those communities actually lived.

mena-mesopotamia.why: One window and one pool covered 3000 BCE to 539 CE, which flattens Sumerian, Akkadian, Assyrian and Babylonian into a single undifferentiated tradition and then runs it a thousand years past the Achaemenid conquest. Split by language and by which city held the plain.

mena-anatolia.why: Bronze Age Anatolia was given Persian and Greek names, both of which arrive centuries too early. The Hittite and Luwian archive at Hattusa is large and dated; use it for the period it covers.

mena-levant.why: The Bronze and Iron Age Levant was given Mesopotamian names, which is the wrong language family. Canaanite, and then Phoenician on the coast, is what the inscriptions hold; Hebrew belongs to the Iron Age kingdoms, not to 3000 BCE.

mena-persian-plateau.why: Persian names began at 1500 BCE, covering Elam — a different language with a two-thousand-year written record at Susa — with the speech of people who had not yet arrived on the plateau.

mena-nubian-corridor.why: One window covered 3000 BCE to 785 CE. Kerma, the Egyptian occupation, Napata and Kush, and Meroe are four different situations; at minimum the Egyptian centuries should use Egyptian names of the right period.

north-american-great-lakes.why: Copied from the Northeast Woodlands, whose present-day window names seven traditions at equal weight. The Great Lakes took Anglophone settlement first, with the German, Irish and Polish waves behind it.

north-american-greenland.why: Copied from the Arctic, which carries Russian and Scandinavian settler pools at the same weight as Inuit. Greenland is Kalaallit with a Danish administration, and never had the others.

north-american-aleutians.why: Same copy, different colonists: Russian America to 1867, American since.

south-american-mato-grosso.why: Copied from the Chaco and Pampas, where the Italian and German waves weigh as much as Spanish. Mato Grosso is Brazilian and its interior is Guarani and Bororo country.

european-azores-and-madeira.why: Copied from Iberia, which splits evenly between Castilian, Portuguese and Galician. These islands were settled from Portugal.

north-american-hudson-bay.why: HPG stopped Hudson Bay at 1600, so every year after it fell outward to the circumpolar Arctic box and drew Russian and Scandinavian names on James Bay while dropping Cree entirely. The bay is Cree to the south and west and Inuit along the northern and eastern coast, and from 1670 the posts add an Orkney, Highland Scots and French-Canadian stock that becomes Metis and country-born families.

deepTime._comment: Correcting the era floors left a hole under every region: the first attested tradition now starts late, and everything earlier fell through to one global invented-syllable pool. The porter fills that hole per region with the deep-time pool for its culture, running from the beginning of time up to whatever year the region's own earliest plausible option begins. Regions settled late are excluded, because there is nobody there to name.

settledFrom._comment: Places reached late by people. A deep-time window here would invent inhabitants; the region is simply uncovered before this year.

weights._comment: Most windows came across giving every tradition equal weight, so a window listing six traditions made a sixth of the population each. These are proportions for populating a scene — legible approximations of the majority-minority shape of a place, not census figures. A tradition left out of an entry keeps weight 1. Keyed by region id, then by the window's start year.

backstops._comment: The atlas is a patchwork of rectangles and people live in the cracks between them: Neijiang sat in a seven-degree gap between west China and south China, and Xi'an, Kunming, Dhaka and Kabul in gaps of their own, all falling through to invented syllables in the middle of literate empires. These are deliberately enormous boxes covering a whole culture zone. The resolver takes the smallest box containing a point, so a backstop only ever wins where nothing better exists, and adding a real region for a place automatically supersedes it. Windows are coarse on purpose; they are the floor, not the answer.
